subject.title: fix(ui): prevent unsafe custodian nudge answers

question: Should Custodian retain a post-send `GatewayRequestError` as uncertain by default, or should the gateway add an explicit non-execution contract before the UI restores a wizard answer or health nudge?
rationale: The correct choice defines the no-replay safety boundary across client transport and server handler execution; the existing generic error type does not establish whether side effects occurred.

options.title: Preserve post-send uncertainty
options.body: Treat every error after `onSent` as unknown and keep the UI blocked until authoritative state resolves it; this is the safest narrow repair.

options.title: Add explicit non-execution metadata
options.body: Extend the gateway error contract only if it can reliably distinguish failures before handler execution from failures after side effects.

options.title: Accept replay risk
options.body: Keep the current rejection classification only with an explicit maintainer decision that duplicate wizard or nudge execution is acceptable.

recommendation.title: Preserve post-send uncertainty
recommendation.body: Treat every error after `onSent` as unknown and keep the UI blocked until authoritative state resolves it; this is the safest narrow repair.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current cross-boundary delivery classification and its regression coverage.
